title: Test the HTTP boundary
summary: Map cart responses to explicit success and failure results, then design tests that cover unauthorized, failed, and malformed responses.

scenario.briefing: The cart summary shows an empty cart for every failure. The team wants the response mapping tested before changing the service again.

objectives.description: Map status and body values to explicit results.
Select the HTTP boundary cases that need tests.

hints: Check the status before trusting the body.
Map every other 4xx and 5xx to a request failure.
Reject a success body that is not an array.

misconceptions.description: Returning success without reading the status.
misconceptions.testDescription: A 401 response asks the user to sign in.
misconceptions.feedback: A response body is only meaningful for a successful status. Check the status first so an error page is not parsed as cart data.

misconceptions.description: Casting any body to an array.
misconceptions.testDescription: A non-array success body is rejected.
misconceptions.feedback: TypeScript casts do not validate JSON. Check Array.isArray before returning success or the template will fail on a non-array value.
The failures are the behavior users report. A suite that only covers 200 never proves the 401, 5xx, or malformed-body branches.

sections.title: HTTP is a boundary
sections.body: HttpClient returns an observable, but the status and body still need interpretation. Map 401, 5xx, and malformed payloads to explicit results before the component renders them.

sections.title: Test the mapper, not the network
sections.body: A pure response mapper can be tested with status and body values. That covers the failure paths without a TestBed, an interceptor, or a live server.

sections.title: TestBed tests need async care
sections.body: A component test that subscribes must await the observable or use a fixture that resolves it. A synchronous assertion often checks the loading state and passes for the wrong reason.

steps.explanation: The mapper has four observable outcomes: success, unauthorized, general failure, and malformed success. A happy-path-only suite and raw HttpResponse assertions do not prove those branches.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Use the editor with Tab and run checks with Ctrl+Enter; every result is announced in text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Tab moves between the editor, hints, and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks. Hint buttons reveal one level at a time.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, pass or fail state, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.
